problem: A curve has parametric equations $x=\frac{{t}^{5}}{5}-2,\,y={t}^{7}+2.$ Given that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=7{t}^{2},$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ at the point where $t=2.$

feedback.problem: A curve has parametric equations $x=2{e}^{t},\,y={e}^{2t}.$ Given that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{t},$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ at the point where $t=3.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}},$ we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}={e}^{t},$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(2{e}^{t})=2{e}^{t}.
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}({e}^{t})}{2{e}^{t}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{2{e}^{t}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ is constant, we get

$$
{\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}|}_{t=3}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$
